bluefintuna: An Atlantic bluefin tuna, a single large torpedo-shaped fish alone, deep metallic blue back and silver flanks, a row of small yellow finlets running along the top and bottom of the tail stalk, a stiff crescent-shaped tail, small pectoral fins folded flat against the body, swimming level
chubmackerel: A single chub mackerel alone, a small streamlined fish about the length of a forearm, steel-blue back marked with dark wavy vertical bars, silver-white belly, deeply forked tail, small finlets before the tail, swimming level, only one fish in frame, not a school
atlanticherring: A single Atlantic herring alone, a small slender silver fish with a deeply forked tail, large loose scales, one soft dorsal fin set at the middle of the back, blue-green sheen along the back, swimming level, only one fish in frame, not a school
mahimahi: A mahi-mahi dolphinfish, a fish and not a dolphin and not a mammal, brilliant green-gold and electric blue body, a very tall blunt vertical forehead, a long dorsal fin running almost the whole length of the back, deeply forked tail, swimming level
opah: An opah moonfish, a single huge deep-bodied fish as round and flat as a dustbin lid, silver body dappled with small white spots, brilliant crimson-orange fins and jaw, a large round eye ringed in gold, swimming level
oceanicwhitetip: An oceanic whitetip shark, a stocky shark with very long broad round-tipped pectoral fins held out sideways like paddles and a large rounded first dorsal fin, each of those fins tipped with a mottled white patch, bronze-grey back and pale belly, swimming level
blueshark: A blue shark, a very slender long-bodied shark with a long pointed snout, extremely long thin scythe-shaped pectoral fins, a large round eye, deep indigo-blue back grading to a white belly, swimming level
remora: A remora sharksucker, a slender dark grey fish with a flat ridged oval sucking disc on top of its head that looks like the sole of a shoe, low soft fins, a single fish alone with no shark in frame, swimming level
sargassumfrogfish: A sargassum frogfish, a small knobbly fish and not a frog and not an amphibian, mottled gold and brown with ragged weed-like skin flaps all over the body, a wide upturned mouth, arm-like pectoral fins with fingered tips gripping a strand of floating brown seaweed
humboldtsquid: A Humboldt squid, a large muscular deep red squid with a torpedo-shaped mantle, two triangular fins at the pointed tip, eight arms and two longer tentacles spread wide, a large round eye, skin flushed red and white
manowar: A Portuguese man o war siphonophore, a floating sea creature and not a ship and not a boat and not a sailing vessel, a translucent gas-filled float shaped like a crested pasty riding on the surface, iridescent pink and blue along the crest, a dense mass of very long thin blue stinging tentacles trailing straight down beneath it, no wood, no cloth sails, no rigging
northerngannet: A northern gannet, a large seabird with a slender pure white body, black wingtips, a buff-yellow wash over the head and nape, a long pale blue-grey dagger-shaped bill, and a pale eye ringed in blue, wings swept back and body straight as a spear in a dive
sootyshearwater: A sooty shearwater, a medium seabird entirely sooty brown-black with narrow stiff swept-back wings held straight and rigid, a slim dark hooked bill with tube-shaped nostrils along the top, gliding low
stormpetrel: A Wilsons storm petrel, a very small sooty-black seabird no bigger than a swallow, with a square white patch across the rump, short rounded wings, and long thin legs trailing behind showing yellow between the toes, fluttering just above the water
tropicbird: A red-billed tropicbird, a white seabird with fine black barring across the back, a bold black stripe through the eye, a heavy coral-red bill, and two extremely long thin white tail streamers longer than the rest of the bird, in level flight
loggerhead: A loggerhead sea turtle, a sea turtle with a notably large blocky head and heavy jaws, a reddish-brown heart-shaped shell, thick paddle-shaped front flippers spread wide, swimming
oliveridley: An olive ridley sea turtle, a small sea turtle with a nearly circular olive-grey shell, a rounded head much smaller than a loggerheads, two claws on each front flipper, flippers spread wide, swimming
housemouse: A house mouse, a small grey-brown rodent with a pointed snout, large thin rounded ears, black bead eyes, and a naked scaly tail about as long as its head and body together, standing on all four legs, an ordinary small animal, not humanoid, not upright
brownrat: A brown rat, a stocky grey-brown rodent clearly larger than a mouse, with a blunt snout, small thick furred ears, coarse fur, and a thick naked scaly tail a little shorter than its head and body, standing on all four legs, not humanoid, not upright
fieldvole: A field vole, a small round-bodied rodent with a blunt rounded snout, small ears almost buried in shaggy grey-brown fur, tiny eyes, and a very short tail no longer than a third of its body, standing on all four legs, not humanoid
commontoad: A common toad, a squat amphibian with dry olive-brown warty bumpy skin, copper-orange eyes with horizontal pupils, and short sturdy legs, sitting hunched on all fours, not a frog, not smooth-skinned, not wet-looking
grasssnake: A grass snake, a slender olive-green snake with a bold pale yellow and black collar band just behind the head, round pupils, keeled scales, body laid in loose S-curves with the head raised
magpie: A Eurasian magpie, a crow-family bird with a glossy black head, breast and back, a clean white belly and white shoulder patches, an iridescent blue-green sheen along the wings, and a very long graduated black tail longer than its body, standing
skylark: A Eurasian skylark, a streaky sandy-brown ground bird about the size of a sparrow, with a short blunt crest raised on the crown, pale breast finely streaked, white outer tail feathers, and a slender pale bill, head tipped back in song
europeanmole: A European mole, a cylindrical animal covered in black velvet fur with no visible eyes and no visible ears, a pink pointed snout, and enormous outward-facing pink spade-shaped front paws far larger than the hind feet, lying flat on its belly, not upright, not humanoid
europeanbadger: A European badger, a heavy low-slung animal with a broad grizzled grey body, short black legs, and a white head marked with a bold black stripe running through each eye from the snout back to the ear, small rounded ears, standing on all four legs, not a honey badger, not upright
herringgull: A herring gull, a large gull with a clean white head and body, a pale grey back and wings, black wingtips marked with small white spots, a heavy yellow bill with a red spot near the tip of the lower half, and pink legs, standing
bluemussel: A single blue mussel alone, one closed bivalve shell, smooth and glossy blue-black, wedge-shaped, pointed at one end and rounded at the other, marked with fine concentric growth rings, a few fine golden threads at the narrow end, only one shell, not a cluster, not a bed
acornbarnacle: A single acorn barnacle alone, one small hard cone built of chalky white overlapping plates like a tiny volcano, with a diamond-shaped opening at the summit and fine feathery legs reaching out through it, only one barnacle, not a cluster
greenanemone: A giant green anemone, a single sea anemone alone, a thick column-shaped body topped by a dense crown of short blunt tentacles radiating outward, uniform bright emerald green, no face, no eyes, not humanoid
aldabratortoise: An Aldabra giant tortoise, a very large land tortoise with a high domed grey-brown shell, thick scaly elephantine legs with blunt claws, a long neck extended upward and a small blunt head, walking
staghorncoral: A staghorn coral colony, a stony coral and not a deer and not antlers of bone, a cluster of pale golden-brown cylindrical arms forking upward with paler tips, surface textured with tiny pores, no animal, no head, no eyes, no fur
braincoral: A brain coral, a stony coral shaped as a large rounded boulder-like dome, its entire surface covered in deep winding meandering ridges and valleys like a maze, tan and olive green, not an actual brain, no organ, no flesh, no face, no animal
giantclam: A giant clam, one huge bivalve alone with a heavy thick fluted shell whose two halves meet in a wavy zigzag line, and a fleshy mantle between them patterned in electric blue, turquoise and gold spots, mantle exposed, only one clam, not a cluster
pistolshrimp: A pistol snapping shrimp, a small shrimp and not a gun and not a firearm and not a weapon, semi-translucent body banded in orange and white, one greatly enlarged asymmetrical claw as large as the rest of its body held out in front, the other claw tiny, long white antennae, no metal
humpheadwrasse: A humphead Napoleon wrasse, a very large reef fish with a prominent bulging hump on the forehead, thick fleshy lips, an electric blue-green body covered in fine maze-like markings, and two dark lines trailing back from each eye, swimming level
kangaroorat: A kangaroo rat, a small sandy-brown desert rodent and not a kangaroo and not a marsupial and with no pouch, with very large hind feet, small front paws held to the chest, a large head with big black eyes and a blunt snout, fur-lined cheek pouches, and a long tufted tail longer than its body, caught mid-hop
namibbeetle: A Namib desert darkling beetle, a single black beetle alone with a smooth domed rounded shell, long slender legs holding the body high off the ground, head lowered and rear end tilted upward in the fog-basking posture, tiny water droplets beaded across its back
egyptianvulture: An Egyptian vulture, a small vulture with dirty-white plumage, black flight feathers along the trailing edge of the wing, a shaggy spiky white ruff of feathers around the neck, and a bare wrinkled yellow-orange face with a slender hooked bill, standing
bumblebeebat: A bumblebee bat, the smallest bat in the world and not an insect and not a bee, a tiny reddish-brown furred bat with a distinctive pig-like snout and swollen fleshy nose, large ears, no tail, and broad dark wing membranes held half open, an actual mammal with fur, no wings of an insect
giantsquirrel: An Indian giant squirrel, a very large tree squirrel with a deep maroon-purple back, cream underparts and a cream face, rounded tufted ears, and an enormous bushy tail longer than its head and body together, gripping a branch
northernpike: A northern pike, a long torpedo-shaped freshwater fish with a broad flattened duck-bill-shaped snout full of needle teeth, olive-green flanks marked with rows of pale bean-shaped spots, and its single dorsal fin set far back near the tail, swimming level
electriceel: An electric eel, a long thick cylindrical fish and not a true eel, dark slate-grey above with an orange-yellow throat and underside, a small head with a blunt flattened snout and small eyes, no dorsal fin at all, and one long ribbon-like fin running the entire length of the underside, swimming level
honeyguide: A greater honeyguide, a small drab starling-sized bird with a grey-brown back, pale underparts, a short stubby pale pink bill, a black throat patch, and white outer tail feathers, perched
